A1.justification: Both complete 39-page PDFs describe the same switchback-experiment study. The main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–D can be reliably matched, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic and ridesharing-data-based simulations, including estimation errors, bias, standard deviations, and bootstrap confidence-interval results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain these original simulation results, including comparisons of switchback designs and estimators and bootstrap confidence-interval analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same OLS, LSTD, modified LSTD, and DRL procedures, including cross-fitting and marginal importance-ratio estimation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same linear and nonlinear synthetic environments and two 40-day ridesharing datasets for treatment-effect estimation. The evaluated covariance and carryover-effect scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 5 and Appendix C retain the same comparators: sequential importance sampling from Bojinov et al. (2023), the burn-in difference-in-mean estimator from Hu and Wager (2022), and simple importance sampling from Xiong et al. (2024).

E3.justification: The simulation settings, preprocessing, metrics, and procedures are unchanged. Examples include synthetic horizon T = 48, n = 16–52 in increments of four, the same switching intervals, and baseline burn-in b = 1.

E4.justification: The carryover-effect analysis, covariance sensitivity experiments in Figures S1–S2, confidence-interval study in Figure S3, and bias/standard-deviation analyses in Figures S4–S5 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregation over 200 simulations and the same nonparametric-bootstrap confidence intervals, coverage probabilities, and average interval widths. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting information is unchanged.

E6.justification: The reported results and plotted data in Figures 1, 3–6, and S1–S5 are unchanged. Appendix C replaces 'Figure ??' with 'Figure 5', identifying an existing comparison without adding or revising results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Markov assumptions, Theorem 1, Corollaries 1–3, and Appendix D's assumptions, lemmas, derivations, and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about carryover effects and reward-error autocorrelations determining efficient switchback designs across RL estimators, together with the same practitioner workflow.

C2.justification: The explanations involving error cancellation and distribution shift, practical design recommendations, and Appendix B's qualifications for mild, moderate, and severe Markov-assumption violations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C retain the same implementation algorithms, parameter specifications, and bootstrap-generation instructions. Section 5 provides the same code-access information.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged. Expanding the abbreviations in the Zhou et al. (2025) reference title identifies the same work and constitutes a bibliographic wording correction.

P1.justification: v7 changes the author display from 'Yang Ying' to 'Ying Yang', expands one bibliography title, repairs Appendix C's 'Figure ??' reference, and updates the version/date stamp. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Reference links change from black to blue, and several figures receive small placement or spacing adjustments, including Figures 4 and 5. The graphics, axes, legends, and overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Repairing Appendix C's unresolved reference to Figure 5 and making reference links visually identifiable improve navigation, while the author and bibliography edits improve presentation. These are limited editorial gains; the scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
